hook: The pharaoh behind the Great Pyramid, the last Wonder of the Ancient World still standing.

pages.x: Khufu was the son of Sneferu, the pharaoh who built more pyramids than any other, learning by trial and error how to make smooth sides that would not collapse. Khufu became king around 2589 BC, ruling Egypt from Memphis at the height of the Old Kingdom.
pages.cap: His father's Red Pyramid at Dahshur

pages.x: At Giza he built the largest pyramid ever made: about 2.3 million blocks, 146 metres high, its sides lined up almost perfectly with north, south, east and west. For about 3,800 years it was the tallest building on Earth, and it is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

Not slaves. In 2013 archaeologists found the oldest written papyri ever discovered, the diary of an official called Merer. It tells how his team of about 40 men shipped limestone blocks down the Nile to Giza. The builders lived in a town beside the pyramid, ate bread, beer and beef, and were buried with honour near their king's tomb.

pages.t: A tiny statue of a giant king
pages.x: The man who built the biggest monument in Egypt is known from only one certain statue, an ivory figure just 7.5 centimetres tall. It was found at Abydos in 1903 with its head missing. The archaeologist Flinders Petrie had his workers sift the rubble for three weeks until the tiny head turned up.

In 1954 workers found a sealed pit beside the pyramid. Inside lay a ship of cedar wood 43 metres long, taken apart into 1,224 pieces, perhaps meant to carry Khufu through the sky with the sun god. It took years to put back together. It is one of the oldest and best-kept ships in the world.

Khufu's pyramid is the most famous building on Earth, and as much a feat of organisation as of stone: quarries, boats, bakeries and thousands of workers all following one plan. For 4,500 years it has stood for the power of ancient Egypt and the ambition of human builders.
pts: Built the Great Pyramid of Giza
The tallest building on Earth for about 3,800 years
The last Wonder of the Ancient World still standing
